slot.brief: Given the temperature of a gas, compute the average translational kinetic energy per molecule using (3/2)kT.

stem: An ideal gas is at a temperature of $400$ K. Taking Boltzmann’s constant as $1.38\times10^{-23}$ J K$^{-1}$, what is the average translational kinetic energy per molecule?

verdicts.working: Average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\frac{3}{2}kT = \frac{3}{2}(1.38\times10^{-23})(400) = 8.28\times10^{-21}$ J.

working:
$$\langle K\rangle=\dfrac{3}{2}kT=\dfrac{3}{2}(1.38\times10^{-23})(400)=8.28\times10^{-21}\ \text{J}$$

Independent check: Average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\frac{3}{2}kT = \frac{3}{2}(1.38\times10^{-23})(400) = 8.28\times10^{-21}$ J.
solution:
For an ideal gas, the average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\langle K\rangle=\frac{3}{2}kT$.
$$\langle K\rangle=\frac{3}{2}(1.38\times10^{-23})(400)=8.28\times10^{-21}\ \text{J}$$
